Consent / DSR / OTI denials (403,409,410) by code
Audit chain: unsealed rows (THE ALARM)
panels.description: THREAT-MODEL calls this the alarm for the async sealing window: rows here carry no chain hash, so verify-audit cannot cover them and an anchor does not attest them. It should oscillate near zero. A value that does not come back down means the sealer is dead or crash-looping - under SUNDER_AUDIT_SEAL_EXTERNAL that is the `sunder sealer` process. Paired with the SunderAuditSealerStalled and SunderAuditSealerStopped alert rules.

panels.title: Erasure notifications stuck (SENDING) / abandoned (FAILED)
panels.description: Article 19 downstream notifications. SENDING means a worker claimed the event and has not recorded an outcome; it should be transient. A persistent value means the scopes that hold the person's records are not being told to delete them. FAILED (the second series) means an endpoint exhausted its attempts - that scope still holds the data.

panels.title: Key material minted at runtime
panels.description: `sunder bootstrap` is the only legitimate source, and it is not `serve`. Any non-zero value on a serving process means the keystore volume is lost, unmounted or pointed at the wrong path: data written under the missing versions is unreadable. Stop the replica and restore the correct keystore before writing anything further.

panels.title: Rate-limit backend failures (Redis)
panels.description: Every limiter decision that fell back because Redis was unreachable. Security-critical buckets (authfail:, share-public:, portal:, claims:, audit-*) fail CLOSED regardless; the rest follow SUNDER_REDIS_FAIL_CLOSED, which defaults to fail-open. A sustained non-zero rate means abuse control is degraded fleet-wide.
